standard.title: People in my family
standard.description: the people in their family, where they were born and raised, and how they are related to each other
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have informal experience of their family through lived experience. No formal prior HASS curriculum.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students identify the people in their family, where they were born and raised, and explain how family members are related to each other.

nodes.label: Who is in my family
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can name the members of their family and use family relationship terms (mother, father, grandparent, sibling, auntie, uncle, cousin) to describe who they are.
nodes.minimum_width: Name at least three family members and use at least two relationship terms correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Identify a range of family members across two generations (self, parents/caregivers, grandparents/extended family) and use a variety of relationship terms; acknowledge that families have different structures.
wider: Explore kinship terms used in First Nations Australian families, such as cousin-brother and mother-auntie, and discuss how family structure and naming differs across cultures
Compare family structures across the class, noting similarities and differences (nuclear, single-parent, extended, blended, grandparent-led)
nodes.hinge_reason: Students who cannot name and relate family members cannot build the concept map or personal narrative required in subsequent nodes — the social organisational vocabulary is the foundation.

response_modes.reason: Students need to build a working vocabulary of relationship terms before they can use them to describe connections. Use photos, drawings and family member visits to build range.

success_criteria: Names at least three people in their family using correct relationship terms
Distinguishes between immediate and extended family members

nodes.label: Where family members were born and raised
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify where key family members were born and raised, and locate these places on a simple map or describe them in relative terms.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify the birthplace or hometown of at least one parent or grandparent and describe it using basic location language (near/far, same place/different place).
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe where two or more family members were born and raised; represent these places on a pictorial map or drawing; use terms like near, far, same city, different country.
wider: Investigate families with connections to countries outside Australia and locate those countries on a globe or world map
Compare family origin stories and discuss why people move to different places

response_modes.reason: Birthplace and origin vary enormously across a class — use this diversity to broaden understanding of where families come from and what 'place' means.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The diversity of birthplaces across a Foundation class offers rich opportunity to explore place and movement; this connects geography to personal identity in a concrete, emotionally significant way.
success_criteria: Identifies where at least one family member was born or raised
Uses at least one location term to describe that place relative to where they live now

nodes.label: How family members are related
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain how two or more family members are connected to each other, using relationship terms and a visual representation such as a concept map or family drawing.
nodes.minimum_width: Explain how at least two family members are related to them and to each other (e.g. 'My grandma is my mum's mum').
nodes.typical_width: Construct a concept map or drawing showing connections between self and multiple family members across two generations; label relationships using appropriate terms.
wider: Explore how First Nations Australian kinship systems describe relationships that extend beyond nuclear family structures
Compare how family relationship terms differ across languages spoken in the class community

response_modes.reason: This node brings together vocabulary from Node 1 and place knowledge from Node 2 into a coherent personal narrative — the concept map is the integration task.

success_criteria: Explains how at least two family members are related to themselves
Produces a visual representation (drawing, concept map, photograph arrangement) showing family connections
